docs.title: About Me
docs.text:
Independent cybersecurity practitioner based in Southern California, with over four years of self-directed study and hands-on technical implementation across security operations, detection engineering, and IT infrastructure.

I hold the CISSP Associate of ISC2 and CompTIA CySA+ certifications, and I maintain an active homelab environment where I build, train, experiment, and document the work that fills this portfolio. My approach is methodical; I read the textbooks, study the research, and then implement it. That cycle informs everything here.

My long-term focus is purple team operations. I believe that deep fluency in both offensive and defensive fundamentals produces better practitioners in either discipline, and that the most effective security work happens at the intersection of both. Along with the technical side, I understand that security exists to serve the business and keep people safe. Risk decisions are business and safety decisions, and effective security practitioners communicate in both languages.

I am currently seeking an entry-level SOC Analyst or security operations role, ideally within a MSSP or an organization with a clear security-focused growth track. I bring verified credentials, documented hands-on work, and the kind of self-driven development that doesn't ever stop.

docs.title: Host-Based Firewall Audit
docs.text: Audit of UFW configurations across NEXUS VMs. Perimeter and inter-VLAN enforcement is handled by pfSense. Host-based firewall provides a secondary enforcement layer on applicable hosts. VMs not listed either do not have UFW installed (Metasploitable2 by design) or rely solely on pfSense perimeter enforcement.

docs.title: Jumpbox (VLAN40)
docs.text:
Default policy: deny incoming, allow outgoing

Port Action Source Notes 22/tcp ALLOW IN 10.0.99.0/24 SSH from management VLAN only 10.0.40.10 22/tcp ALLOW OUT ens18 SSH to REMnux 10.0.40.20 22/tcp ALLOW OUT ens18 SSH to FlareVM

Outbound SSH scoped explicitly to analysis workstation IPs. No unrestricted outbound permitted.

docs.title: REMnux (VLAN40)
docs.text:
Default policy: deny incoming, deny outgoing

Port Action Source Notes 22/tcp ALLOW IN 10.0.40.2 SSH from Jumpbox only Anywhere ALLOW IN 10.0.40.20 FlareVM analysis collaboration

Default deny on outgoing reflects malware analysis workstation posture, prevents inadvertent outbound connections during sample detonation. Ingress restricted to Jumpbox and FlareVM exclusively.

docs.title: pfSense Firewall Rule Configuration
docs.text: Per-VLAN firewall rules enforced by pfSense. Rules are processed top-down, first match wins. Block rules are explicit; pfSense denies all unmatched traffic by default. Screenshots for each VLAN are included below each section.

docs.title: LAN (VLAN99 - SOC Management)
docs.text:
Default policy: implicit deny (unmatched traffic)

Rule Protocol Source Destination Port Action Anti-Lockout * * LAN Address 443, 80 Pass Allow Admin SSH to Jumpbox TCP 10.0.99.0/24 10.0.40.2 22 Pass Block LAN to home network IPv4 * LAN subnets 192.168.0.0/24 * Block Default allow LAN to any IPv4 * LAN subnets * * Pass Default allow LAN IPv6 IPv6 * LAN subnets * * Pass

SSH access to the air gap segment is restricted to the Jumpbox only, no direct management access to REMnux or FlareVM from VLAN99. The anti-lockout rule is a pfSense system rule preventing administrative lockout.

docs.title: VLAN10 - AD Environment
docs.text:
Default policy: implicit deny

Rule Protocol Source Destination Port Action Allow gateway IPv4 * VLAN10 subnets This Firewall * Pass Block to home network IPv4 * VLAN10 subnets 192.168.0.0/24 * Block Block to VLAN40 IPv4 * VLAN10 subnets VLAN40 subnets * Block Allow all VLAN10 traffic IPv4 * VLAN10 subnets * * Pass

Target environment with broad outbound access. VLAN40 explicitly blocked to prevent target VMs from reaching the malware analysis segment.

docs.title: VLAN20 - DevSecOps
docs.text:
Default policy: implicit deny

Rule Protocol Source Destination Port Action Allow gateway IPv4 * VLAN20 subnets This Firewall * Pass Block to home network IPv4 * VLAN20 subnets 192.168.0.0/24 * Block Block to VLAN40 IPv4 * VLAN20 subnets VLAN40 subnets * Block Allow VLAN20 internal networks IPv4 * VLAN20 subnets 10.0.0.0/8 * Pass Allow VLAN20 Internet IPv4 * VLAN20 subnets * * Pass

IaC tooling segment. DevSecOps tooling requires internet access for package management and module downloads.

docs.title: VLAN40 - Air Gap Segment
docs.text:
Default policy: implicit deny

Rule Protocol Source Destination Port Action Block to home network IPv4 * 10.0.40.0/24 192.168.0.0/24 * Block Block to all internal networks IPv4 * 10.0.40.0/24 10.0.0.0/8 * Block Block to Internet IPv4 * 10.0.40.0/24 * * Block

Fully isolated malware analysis segment. No outbound traffic permitted to any destination. Ingress controlled exclusively at the host level via Jumpbox SSH. pfSense enforces complete network isolation, UFW on REMnux and FlareVM provides secondary host-level enforcement.

docs.title: VLAN50 - Adversary Emulation
docs.text:
Default policy: implicit deny

Rule Protocol Source Destination Port Action Allow intra-subnet IPv4 * VLAN50 subnets 10.0.50.0/24 * Pass Allow reverse shell callbacks to VLAN99 IPv4 TCP VLAN50 subnets 10.0.99.0/24 * Pass Block to home network IPv4 * VLAN50 subnets 192.168.0.0/24 * Block Block to all internal networks IPv4 * VLAN50 subnets 10.0.0.0/8 * Block Block Internet access IPv4 * VLAN50 subnets * * Block

Adversary emulation segment hosting Metasploitable2. Reverse shell callback rule placed above the internal block rule. Internet access blocked entirely. Metasploitable2 is an intentionally vulnerable image and must not reach external networks under any circumstances.

docs.title: VLAN70 - AI Backend
docs.text:
Default policy: implicit deny

Rule Protocol Source Destination Port Action Allow DNS IPv4 TCP/UDP VLAN70 subnets * 53 Pass Allow HTTPS IPv4 TCP VLAN70 subnets * 443 Pass Allow HTTP IPv4 TCP VLAN70 subnets * 80 Pass Allow gateway IPv4 * 10.0.70.0/24 This Firewall * Pass Block 192.168.0.0/16 IPv4 * 10.0.70.0/24 192.168.0.0/16 * Block Block to internal networks IPv4 * 10.0.70.0/24 10.0.0.0/8 * Block Block all outbound IPv4 * VLAN70 subnets * * Block

Ollama inference engine requires internet access for model pulls via HTTP/HTTPS. All other outbound traffic blocked. n8n-to-Ollama API traffic (port 11434) is permitted via the default LAN allow rule on VLAN99. No additional rule required on VLAN70 due to stateful inspection handling return traffic.

docs.title: Post-Quantum Cryptography
docs.text: Resource Description Link CRYSTALS-Kyber An IND-CCA2-secure key encapsulation mechanism (KEM) whose security is based on the hardness of the learning-with-errors (LWE) problem over module lattices. Standardized as FIPS 203 (ML-KEM). ↗ CRYSTALS-Dilithium A digital signature scheme strongly secure under chosen message attacks, based on the hardness of lattice problems over module lattices. Standardized as FIPS 204 (ML-DSA). ↗ FALCON A lattice-based digital signature scheme grounded in the NTRU lattice problem, using Fast Fourier sampling for compact, efficient signatures. Standardized as FIPS 206 (FN-DSA). ↗ SPHINCS+ A stateless hash-based signature scheme offering conservative security with no reliance on structured lattice assumptions. Standardized as FIPS 205 (SLH-DSA). ↗ BIKE A Round 4 KEM candidate under NIST evaluation, based on quasi-cyclic moderate-density parity-check (QC-MDPC) codes. ↗ HQC A Round 4 KEM candidate under NIST evaluation, based on the hardness of decoding random quasi-cyclic codes (code-based cryptography). ↗
